tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.description:
Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework.

You must call 'Resolve Context7 Library ID' tool first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question.

If you know the programming language the user is working in, pass it as `language` so the results match their setup.

libraryId.description: Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., '/mongodb/docs', '/vercel/next.js', '/supabase/supabase', '/vercel/next.js/v16.2.9') retrieved from 'resolve-library-id' or directly from user query in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version'.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation, scoped to a single concept. Be specific and include relevant details, but keep each query to one topic — if the user's question spans multiple distinct concepts, make a separate call per concept instead of combining them, unless the question is about how the concepts interact. Good: 'How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js' or 'React useEffect cleanup function examples'. Bad (too vague): 'auth' or 'hooks'. Bad (too broad): 'routing and auth and caching in Next.js'. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Context7__resolve-library-id
tools.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation. This is used to rank library results by relevance to what the user is trying to accomplish. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

entries.description: Get the Quality Gate Status for a project. Either 'analysisId', 'projectId' or 'projectKey' must be provided.

projectKey.description: The optional project key to get the status for, for example 'my_project'

analysisId.description: The optional analysis ID to get the status for, for example 'AU-TpxcA-iU5OvuD2FL1'

branch.description: Long-lived branch name in SonarQube (e.g. 'main', 'develop'). Use list_branches to discover valid names. Not for feature branches or pull request analysis — use pullRequest instead.

projectId.description: The optional project ID to get the status for, for example 'AU-Tpxb--iU5OvuD2FLy'. Doesn't work with branches or pull requests.

pullRequest.description: Pull request key/ID in SonarQube. Use list_pull_requests to discover valid keys. Not for long-lived branches — use branch instead. Must be the SonarQube PR key, not a git branch name.

entries.name: mcp__sonarqube-anchildress1__list_branches
entries.description: List long-lived branches for a project (e.g. main, develop, master). Use returned branch names as the branch parameter on other tools (e.g. get_project_quality_gate_status, get_component_measures). For pull requests, use list_pull_requests instead.

projectKey.description: The SonarQube project key (e.g. my_project). Use search_my_sonarqube_projects when the key is unknown.

entries.name: mcp__sonarqube-anchildress1__list_pull_requests
entries.description: List all pull requests for a project. Use this tool to discover available pull requests and their corresponding branch names before analyzing their coverage, issues, or quality. Returns the pull request key/ID and source branch for each PR, which can be used with other tools that accept a pullRequest parameter. For long-lived branches (main, develop), use list_branches instead.

projectKey.description: The SonarQube project key (e.g. my_project). Use search_my_sonarqube_projects when the key is unknown.

entries.name: mcp__sonarqube-anchildress1__search_security_hotspots
entries.description: Search for Security Hotspots in a project.

p.description: An optional page number. Defaults to 1.

projectKey.description: The key of the project or application to search in. Required unless hotspotKeys is provided.

ps.description: An optional page size. Must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 500. Defaults to 100.

onlyMine.description: If true, only Security Hotspots assigned to the current user are returned

hotspotKeys.description: Comma-separated list of specific Security Hotspot keys to retrieve. Required unless projectKey is provided.

files.description: An optional list of file paths to filter Security Hotspots

sinceLeakPeriod.description: If true, only Security Hotspots created since the leak period (new code period) are returned

resolution.description: Filter by resolution (when status is REVIEWED)

input.description: Fix pages.ts Codex findings
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/anchildress1/git_personal/gravespeaker (SvelteKit 3, TypeScript strict, ESM, pnpm). Run every pnpm command with `VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1` set in the env.

Task: fix two real bugs reported by a code reviewer in src/lib/server/pages.ts (tests in src/lib/server/pages.test.ts). Do not touch any other source file.

Context: `fetchPage(url)` fetches a source page for a story. Internals: `guardedFetch` (manual redirects, max 3 hops, each hop SSRF-checked and DNS-pinned via an undici Agent), `readCapped` (reads body up to 2 MB), robots.txt check via robots-parser for UA "Gravespeaker". Keep the SSRF/DNS-pinning behavior exactly intact.

Bug 1: "If a source or its robots.txt sends headers but then stalls past the 8 s timeout or resets the connection, `reader.read()` in `readCapped` rejects outside any catch. The exception escapes `fetchPage`, so the snippet fallback in story.ts never runs and `Promise.all` rejects the whole fetch step." Fix: body-read failures must make that page unavailable (`fetchPage` returns null), never throw. For a failing robots.txt body read, treat robots as unavailable the same way a missing robots.txt is treated today (allow). Think about which is right and keep consistent with existing behavior for non-OK robots.txt.

Bug 2: "Robots permission is checked only for the original URL. When an allowed URL redirects to a disallowed path or another site's disallowed page, `guardedFetch(url)` follows redirects without consulting robots at the destination." Fix: apply the robots check for every redirect destination (same-origin or cross-origin) before fetching it. Suggested shape: give `guardedFetch` an optional per-hop `allowed(url: URL) => Promise<boolean>` callback that `fetchPage` supplies for the page request (fetching/parsing robots.txt for each hop's origin, reusing a small per-call cache keyed by origin so the same origin is not fetched twice); the robots.txt fetch itself should not recurse into robots checks. A disallowed hop makes the result null.

Add tests to src/lib/server/pages.test.ts (existing style: stub globalThis.fetch + mock node:dns/promises; behavior assertions, no "mock was called" assertions except where the existing DNS-pin test already does):
- body stream that errors mid-read -> `fetchPage` resolves null (does not throw)
- robots.txt body that errors mid-read -> page still fetched (allowed) and does not throw
- allowed URL redirecting to a path disallowed by robots.txt -> null
- allowed URL redirecting to another public host whose robots.txt disallows -> null
- redirect to an allowed destination -> text returned

Rules: JSDoc on every function/method/class (eslint-plugin-jsdoc enforces it); inline comments only for WHY; no new dependencies; keep the existing `// NOSONAR` and `// nosemgrep` markers on their lines; do NOT commit, push, or run `make ai-checks` / coverage (other agents edit other files in the same working tree).

input.description: Fix narrative sentence validation
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/anchildress1/git_personal/gravespeaker (SvelteKit 3, TypeScript strict, ESM, pnpm). Run every pnpm command with `VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1` set in the env.

Task: fix a real grounding bug in src/lib/server/narrative.ts (`groundStory`), tests in src/lib/server/narrative.test.ts. Touch no other source file.

Reviewer finding (valid): "When the model supplies a real quote alongside an unsupported sentence, the check accepts the sentence as a documented fact without checking whether the quote supports it. input.description: Fix pages.ts Codex findings
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/anchildress1/git_personal/gravespeaker (SvelteKit 3, TypeScript strict, ESM, pnpm). Run every pnpm command with `VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1` set in the env.

Task: fix two real bugs reported by a code reviewer in src/lib/server/pages.ts (tests in src/lib/server/pages.test.ts). Do not touch any other source file.

Context: `fetchPage(url)` fetches a source page for a story. Internals: `guardedFetch` (manual redirects, max 3 hops, each hop SSRF-checked and DNS-pinned via an undici Agent), `readCapped` (reads body up to 2 MB), robots.txt check via robots-parser for UA "Gravespeaker". Keep the SSRF/DNS-pinning behavior exactly intact.

Bug 1: "If a source or its robots.txt sends headers but then stalls past the 8 s timeout or resets the connection, `reader.read()` in `readCapped` rejects outside any catch. The exception escapes `fetchPage`, so the snippet fallback in story.ts never runs and `Promise.all` rejects the whole fetch step." Fix: body-read failures must make that page unavailable (`fetchPage` returns null), never throw. For a failing robots.txt body read, treat robots as unavailable the same way a missing robots.txt is treated today (allow). Think about which is right and keep consistent with existing behavior for non-OK robots.txt.

Bug 2: "Robots permission is checked only for the original URL. When an allowed URL redirects to a disallowed path or another site's disallowed page, `guardedFetch(url)` follows redirects without consulting robots at the destination." Fix: apply the robots check for every redirect destination (same-origin or cross-origin) before fetching it. Suggested shape: give `guardedFetch` an optional per-hop `allowed(url: URL) => Promise<boolean>` callback that `fetchPage` supplies for the page request (fetching/parsing robots.txt for each hop's origin, reusing a small per-call cache keyed by origin so the same origin is not fetched twice); the robots.txt fetch itself should not recurse into robots checks. A disallowed hop makes the result null.

Add tests to src/lib/server/pages.test.ts (existing style: stub globalThis.fetch + mock node:dns/promises; behavior assertions, no "mock was called" assertions except where the existing DNS-pin test already does):
- body stream that errors mid-read -> `fetchPage` resolves null (does not throw)
- robots.txt body that errors mid-read -> page still fetched (allowed) and does not throw
- allowed URL redirecting to a path disallowed by robots.txt -> null
- allowed URL redirecting to another public host whose robots.txt disallows -> null
- redirect to an allowed destination -> text returned

content.text:
All 17 Sonar issues and the three Codex findings are fixed in 8 local commits, and the gate is green. I haven't pushed, so I haven't replied to or resolved any PR thread yet. `make ai-checks` passes with 108 tests. A live story run still returned a "told" story with real facts and imagined lines, and I haven't re-run Sonar.

## Reviewer presence
- **Copilot:** no review on PR #5. I didn't diagnose why, since it isn't a required reviewer here.
- **Codex:** reviewed, with 3 threads.
- **Other reviewers:** CodeQL, SonarCloud and Semgrep.

## Threads (4)
- **CodeQL, substring URL check:** fixed. The test stub now compares the exact hostname. The reply and resolution wait for the push.
- **Codex P1, a fact's sentence wasn't checked against its quote:** fixed. A fact is dropped if it adds a number, number word, proper noun or mostly new words beyond its quote. Spelled-out numbers match digits. Six tests cover it, including the reviewer's reproduction.
- **Codex P2, body failures escaped the snippet fallback:** fixed. A page or `robots.txt` body that fails mid-read now makes that source unavailable, so the fallback runs.
- **Codex P2, `robots.txt` was checked only for the first URL:** fixed. It's checked at every redirect hop, once per origin.

## Sonar (17 issues, no hotspots)
- **Deprecated `json` helper (8):** replaced with `Response.json`.
- **Complexity, sort, regex backtracking, redundant type alias, nested ternary (5):** fixed.
- **Async step with no `await` (2):** fixed.
- **"Prefer top-level await" (2):** I put `NOSONAR` on the last `.then(...)` in each workflow chain, with a reason. That `.then` is Mastra's builder, not a Promise. I put the markers on the last `.then(...)` after correcting an off-by-one; I believe that's the line Sonar flags but can't confirm until it re-runs.

## Title and description
Left unchanged for now. It says 91 unit tests, and it's now 108 with the new fixes. I'll update it after the push so it matches what's on the branch.

## Self-review
I ran `/code-review` and got 9 findings.
- **Fixed:**
  - Number words versus digits.
  - A proper noun opening a sentence.
  - Short theatrical lines such as "Come closer." were being dropped, and longer label lines such as "Reconstruction line one:" were slipping through.
  - `robots.txt` now follows RFC 9309: a 5xx, a failed fetch or a broken body skips the page.
  - The duplicated date helper is now shared.
- **Not fixed, with a reason:**
  - **Synchronous throw in a step:** I tested it, and a throw still becomes a `failed` run.
  - **Extra `robots.txt` request per new origin:** it goes through the same SSRF-checked, DNS-pinned fetch, so it's a small extra request, not a bypass.
  - **Prompt example lost its `(quote: …)` marker:** the output schema and rules already require quotes, and live runs kept the facts.
  - **Regex change as a drive-by:** it was a requested Sonar fix, and its tests are unchanged.

## Needs your input
- **Entire Gates:** this check fails on "no approvals" and "CI checks have not passed". It clears once CodeQL passes and someone approves.
- **`robots.txt` fail-closed:** flaky `robots.txt` sites now fall back to the search snippet instead of the full page. That's the RFC behavior, but your call if you'd rather fail open.

## Status
8 new commits on top of the pushed branch: 5 for Sonar and Codex, 2 for the self-review, and 1 for CodeQL. Together with the two README commits, none are pushed. Say "push" and I'll push, then reply to and resolve the four threads, update the description, and post the self-review marker.

content.text:
The fact check is now strict enough to close the gap, and it's committed as `cd75781` (not pushed). `make ai-checks` passes with 113 tests.

## What changed
- **Claim words:** every claim word in a fact must come from its quote, in the quote's order, with number words equal to digits.
- **Negations:** a negation the quote doesn't contain is rejected.
- **Prompt:** the model is told to restate the quote's own words in the first person and put all flair in the imagined lines.
- **Tests added:** "famous pianist" and "never taught piano" are dropped. So are an invented "to the whole county" and a reordered sentence. "Arthur preceded me in death", a reversal of the quote, is dropped too.

## Live check
Two story runs came back "told" with real, quote-faithful facts (born date, piano for forty years, preceded by husband Arthur, the large garden). A third run failed with a lookup-service error, probably free-tier rate limiting after my repeated test calls; I didn't confirm.

## Limits
It still compares wording, not meaning. A fact that reuses the quote's words in order but swaps a single word could pass. The note's stricter option, showing the quote beside each fact, remains available if you want a guarantee. I left it out because it changes the UI.

## Your other questions
- **Approving your own PR:** you can't, so the Entire "Approvals" gate can't pass on your own account. That's a policy question for that tool, not something I can fix in code.
- **Flaky `robots.txt` sites:** I have no evidence of any. Nine of ten common record sites answered 200 in about 0.1–0.3 s. tributearchive.com answered 403, which counts as no rules. Fail-closed only triggers on 5xx, timeouts or broken bodies.

## Status
9 commits are local and unpushed. Say "push" and I'll push, then reply to and resolve the four threads, update the description, and post the self-review marker.

cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-anchildress1-git-personal-gravespeaker/092a50a5-6a5a-4fe0-8c45-dcc2512da7ab/scratchpad/pr.md <<'EOF'
## What

The full MVP journey (spec `001-mvp-journey`): photograph a headstone, confirm who it is, hear a theatrical first-person story built from cited public records.

## How it works

- **Read:** Gemma 4 26B (via Mastra) reads the name and life dates. Code normalizes the output: honorifics, `née` split into a maiden-name signal, `?` for worn digits, letterless names dropped. A surname carved once on a shared stone applies to both people.
- **Research:** SerpApi search, paywalled sites filtered, Gemma groups hits into people. Code drops hits that never name the surname, dates no source states, sources claimed by two people, and year conflicts.
- **Story:** the confirmed candidate's pages are fetched and Gemma performs an openly fictional ghost monologue. Code keeps a fact only if its quote appears in a cited source and its sentence restates that quote: no new number, proper noun or negation, and every claim word in the quote's order. No fact beyond the name and dates means the stone-only epitaph, never an AI story.
- **Page fetch guard:** public addresses only, DNS pinned to the checked address, redirects re-checked, `robots.txt` honored at every hop. An unreachable, 5xx or unreadable `robots.txt` skips the page (RFC 9309) and the story uses the search snippet.

## Verification

- `make ai-checks` and `make e2e` pass: 113 unit tests, 12 Playwright tests on a 390 px viewport. Coverage of app logic is about 97% of statements.
- Benchmark run 11 (21 reviewed stones): 63/64 fields, 3.8 s median. Only the worn Ellis 1818 digit misses. No benchmark runs past 11; prompt changes are tested in the app.
- Semgrep and gitleaks clean. CodeQL and all 17 Sonar issues from the first scan are addressed in this PR.
- Mobile Lighthouse on the preview build: 100 on all four categories.
- Walked through on a desktop and on a phone against the preview server.

## Notes for review

- **New dependencies:** `@mastra/core`, `zod`, `@mozilla/readability`, `linkedom`, `robots-parser`, `undici` (needed to pin DNS). The `serpapi` package was dropped because it uses `https` and can't be mocked at the network boundary.
- **Spec change:** FR-006 no longer says the maiden name is searched. Live searches showed it buried the real record, so it is a read signal only.
- **`Dockerfile`:** `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT` raised from 10M to 12M so a 10 MB photo plus multipart overhead reaches the app's own check. Not yet verified on Cloud Run; nothing is deployed.
- **Fixtures:** the new `holmquist-2024.jpg` is kept out of this PR and stays local for now. The photo already exists in earlier history; this PR only adds its answer key to `fixtures/manifest.json`.
- **Known limits:** the fact check compares wording, not meaning. The SSRF deny-list covers loopback, private, link-local and CGNAT ranges, not multicast, reserved or NAT64 ranges.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
